notes_for_editor: Newspaper search (Chronicling America) timed out under shared rate limits and was not used. Disagreements shown in the text: authorisation 1806 vs 1807; rebuilding authorisation 1830 vs 1831; present tower 1857 vs 1858; steam signal 1868/1869; Johnson's last year 1928/1930/1931; transfer to the state 1986 (Keeper's Log) vs 1998 (Lighthousefriends). Keeper's Log says the station was automated in 1968, evidently a typo for 1988. Keeper's Log says a radiobeacon was added in the 1920s; the 1932 Bulletin says one was still being planned. The 1929 wreck anecdote is second-hand (a grandson's recollection in Down East via New England Lighthouses) and calls Larrabee assistant when USLHS lists him as head from 1928. The 1884 life-saving report is fiscal 1883-84, so the Ideal was August 1883; the 1888 report is fiscal 1887-88, so the Ontario was July 1887 and the Baston December 1887. Page numbers of the Light-House Board reports for 1895 and 1901 were not determined (no page index); 1899 is cited by scan page. The USLHS roster also lists Coast Guard crew under 'other'; nine names beyond the head keepers were not reconciled with Lighthousefriends (Sneddon/Snedden spelling; Joseph E. Griffeneni, William A. Howland appear only there). The roster lines for Coast Guard crew have no role detail. Story quotes Alfred Godfrey's 1842 statement via Lighthousefriends; the original Lewis report was not read.
